fields.text: Fourth-generation 5.0-liter Coyote V8, naturally aspirated, with dual intake and dual throttle body induction
fields.publisher: Ford Motor Company (From the Road newsroom)
fields.note: Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). Ford's 2024 Mustang GT pace-car release was summarised as describing the 'Mustang GT 5.0-liter V8', a naturally aspirated V8 with a 'segment-first, dual intake and dual throttle body induction system'; Jalopnik's summary called it the fourth-generation 5.0-liter Coyote. The sentence is assembled from those two summaries, not a single verbatim Ford sentence. The card reviewer confirmed only '5.0L Coyote V8' (TFLcar) and did not see 'fourth-generation' or the dual-throttle wording again. The Jalopnik URL is the slug the reviewer saw for the same article id (1849534613); the earlier record used a different slug that may be stale. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11, card key fuelType). The card reviewer's search summarised fueleconomy.gov record 47558 (2024 Mustang, 5.0 L, 8 cyl, manual 6-speed) as showing its MPG under a 'regular gasoline' heading. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.publisher: Ford Motor Company (From the Road newsroom)
fields.note: Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11, card key aspiration = naturally-aspirated). Ford's release was summarised as calling the standard 480 hp GT 'the most standard power in a naturally aspirated V8-powered Mustang ever'. The card reviewer did not see the words again but found nothing contradicting them (superchargers appeared only as aftermarket kits). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 for the 2024 Mustang was summarised as '8 cylinders, 5.0 liters, manual 6-speed'; the card reviewer's fresh search returned the same. Ford's release calls it the 'Mustang GT 5.0-liter V8'. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 was summarised as '8 cylinders, 5.0 liters, manual 6-speed'; confirmed by the card reviewer. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.publisher: Ford Motor Company (From the Road newsroom)
fields.note: Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). Ford's release was summarised as rating the standard Mustang GT at 480 horsepower, with 486 hp only on GT models with the optional active-valve performance exhaust. The card reviewer's TFLcar result agreed (480 standard, 486 with the active exhaust). 480 kept because this configuration names no exhaust option; see conflicts. No rpm for peak power was given. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). Jalopnik was summarised as reporting Ford's figures: 480 hp and 415 lb-ft for the GT without the active-valve exhaust, 486 hp and 418 lb-ft with it. The card reviewer's TFLcar result agreed and said the ratings are the same for the manual and the 10-speed automatic. Ford's own newsroom summary printed only the 418 lb-ft (active exhaust) figure, so the 415 figure is republished, not read on a Ford page. URL is the Jalopnik slug the reviewer saw for article id 1849534613. No rpm for peak torque was given. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). A California DriveClean listing for the 2024 Ford Mustang was summarised as 'Manual 6-spd, 5.0L, Rear-Wheel Drive'. Two DriveClean URLs appeared in those results and the summary did not say which carried the line; this is the first of them, so the URL (not the value) is uncertain. The card reviewer saw no drive layout in its own summaries and nothing contradicting RWD. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 was summarised as 'manual 6-speed' for the 2024 Mustang 5.0L. The card reviewer also saw a tractionlife.com summary describing the standard GT gearbox as a Getrag MT-82 6-speed manual with rev-matching (the 10-speed automatic is optional); that summary did not say which tractionlife page carried the line, so it is not cited as a URL. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11, card key transmission = '6-speed manual'). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 was summarised as '8 cylinders, 5.0 liters, manual 6-speed'. The individual gear ratios and final drive were not in any summary. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.publisher: Ford Motor Company (2024 Mustang Technical Specifications, preliminary; copy hosted by a third party)
fields.note: Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). Search summaries of Ford's 2024 Mustang technical specifications PDF said the GT column gives an estimated curb weight of 3,730 lb for the fastback with the manual (3,752 lb with the automatic). WEAK: the sheet is marked preliminary (as of Sept. 14, 2022, subject to change) and the weight is an estimate; one card reviewer said the summary assigned the figure to the GT column by inference from column order; both URLs are third-party re-hosts of the same Ford PDF, so the corroborating URL is the same document, not a second source; the summary did not say whether the figure excludes the GT Performance Package. Kept as the only maker figure that names this body and transmission; both card reviewers recommended caution. Other published weights run 11 to 217 lb higher; see conflicts. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 (2024 Mustang, 5.0L V8, 6-speed manual) was summarised as 15 city / 23 highway / 18 combined MPG; the card reviewer's fresh search returned the same page and figures (a re-read of the same page, not a second publisher). A California DriveClean listing was also summarised with the same figures, but its URL is uncertain. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 (2024 Mustang, 5.0L V8, 6-speed manual) was summarised as 15 city / 23 highway / 18 combined MPG; confirmed on a re-read by the card reviewer. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). fueleconomy.gov record 47558 (2024 Mustang, 5.0L V8, 6-speed manual) was summarised as 18 combined MPG; confirmed on a re-read by the card reviewer. AutoPadre lists 19; see conflicts. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). MotorBiscuit's spec table for the 2024 Mustang GT was summarised as 'Top speed 155 mph (governed)'; a Roadblazing review (spec box for a GT Premium) gave the same. WEAK: no Ford-published top speed and no measured run was found, the corroborating source is a different trim, and forum reports of the S650 limiter disagree (about 140, 145, 150, 155, 160+); a second card run left this figure out. See conflicts. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11). MotorBiscuit's table was summarised as '155 mph (governed)' for the 2024 Mustang GT, and another review said 'electronically limited'; forum posts also describe an electronic limiter on S650 Mustangs. Not confirmed by Ford; stands or falls with the 155 mph figure. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

TRIM MISMATCH: carried over from the earlier card reviewer's search (2026-11-11), which summarised the Auto123 listing as giving ventilated front discs on the fastback GT, with the 'GT Premium fastback listed with a 13.8 in front rotor'. The figure is for the GT Premium fastback (transmission not stated), not the base GT, and no result said whether base GT and GT Premium share front brakes; the GT Performance Package fits larger Brembo brakes, so this is not the Performance Package size. No Ford figure surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

CONFIGURATION MISMATCH (options): Edmunds' instrumented test was summarised as the GT pulling 0.97 g on the skidpad. The tested car was a 2024 Mustang GT fastback with the 5.0L V8, six-speed manual and RWD (same engine, transmission and drive) but WITH the optional GT Performance Package (summer tires, wider rear tires, Brembo brakes, revised chassis tuning, and per an earlier summary a 3.73 axle), so it is not a base-GT grip figure. The card reviewer confirmed the value and the Performance Package equipment. Edmunds' skidpad diameter was not stated in any summary. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

CONFIGURATION MISMATCH (options): Edmunds' instrumented test was summarised as a 103-foot stop from 60 mph for the GT, the same Performance Package manual fastback as the skidpad figure (larger Brembo brakes and summer tires, not the base GT's). The card reviewer confirmed 103 ft in Edmunds' table but noted a second Edmunds page implying 102 ft for the GT; see conflicts. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

conflicts.note: Kept 480 hp, Ford's standard GT rating. 486 hp is Ford's figure for a GT with the optional active-valve performance exhaust (Ford newsroom, Jalopnik, MotorWeek, The Drive headlines quote it as 'the' GT figure). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 415 lb-ft to match the standard 480 hp rating (Jalopnik reporting Ford, TFLcar, cars.com, Ford Performance crate-engine page). 418 lb-ft applies only with the optional active-valve exhaust and is the only torque figure Ford's newsroom summary printed. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 3,730 lb, the only maker figure naming the GT fastback manual, but it is a preliminary estimate (Ford sheet dated Sept. 14, 2022; automatic 3,752 lb). 3,741 lb 'base curb weight' (Cars.com, CarBuzz, iSeeCars, Motor Matchup, Auto123; transmission not stated; likely one licensed data feed; exactly the midpoint of Ford's manual and automatic estimates). 3,827 lb (Yahoo Autos / The Drive first drive, Motor1 for a GT Premium; one summary pairs it with the 6-speed manual). 3,866 lb (Edmunds test car, GT Performance Package manual; the earlier summary did not give the page, so it is not recorded as testWeightLb). 3,947 lb (MotorBiscuit, said to be the manual; Road Blazing, GT Premium). 3,933 lb (AutoPadre, GT Premium) also appeared. European 446 hp GT figures (about 1,733 kg) are a different market. A modeller should treat curb weight as uncertain by up to about 200 lb. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 155 mph governed (MotorBiscuit spec table; Road Blazing GT Premium spec box; a mustang7g forum post saying the governor is 155 on the GT and 168 on the Dark Horse). Others: 'will top 150 mph' (The Auto Channel review of a manual GT coupe), an estimated 160 mph (Motor1), 145 and about 140 mph limiters (forum posts), 175 mph (Motor Matchup simulation), and 168 mph in an unlabeled KBB column that appears to be the Dark Horse. No Ford or measured figure. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 18 mpg from fueleconomy.gov record 47558 (5.0L 6-speed manual). AutoPadre lists 19. CJ Pony Parts' 15/24/17 appears to be the automatic, and Ford Authority's 14 mpg city is the Dark Horse manual. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. Edmunds' Performance Package manual GT (the test kept for skidpad and braking) was summarised as 4.8 s in one reading and 5.6 s in another of the same article; the card reviewer saw 4.8 s and judged 5.6 s to be the EcoBoost row, but the contradiction was not settled and Edmunds' rollout convention was not stated. MotorTrend 4.3 s (manual GT WITH Performance Package and active exhaust, quoted on a forum). Car and Driver 4.2 s for 'the GT 6-speed' (relayed second-hand by a J.D. Power page, options not stated); a Car and Driver 4.5 s figure was a Performance Package automatic. Consumer Reports 4.6 s (transmission not stated). The Auto Channel about 4.0 s (not clearly instrumented). Motor1 4.5 s was an estimate. No test of a GT without the Performance Package surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Edmunds' 0.97 g because the tested car is identified (GT Performance Package, 6-speed manual fastback). 0.99 g was attributed to Car and Driver's October 2023 issue by a low-reliability mirror site that did not state the tested trim or options. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 103 ft from Edmunds' test table for the Performance Package manual GT. A second Edmunds page says the EcoBoost's 105 ft was '3 feet more than the hardtop GT', implying 102 ft. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. 153 ft from 70 mph was attributed to Car and Driver's October 2023 issue only by a low-reliability mirror site that did not state the tested trim or options. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. 5.3 in came from a single unnamed review in a search summary; 143 mm (about 5.6 in, listed as '6 in') is CarsGuide's figure for the Australian-market GT with the 10-speed automatic; Autopadre's 5.2 to 5.7 in range mixed in Mach-E entries. Cars.com showed no figure for the GT and Ford's spec-sheet summaries did not show one. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
